runs.text: 1. What is an operator in Java?
An operator is a mechanism used to perform a particular operation on data.
Operands are the data or values on which an operator performs an operation.
Technically, an operator performs its operation using one or more operands.
3. How are operators classified based on the number of operands?
Based on the number of operands required to perform an operation, operators are classified into three types:
A unary operator is an operator that requires only one operand to perform an operation.
Each of these operates on a single operand.
A binary operator is an operator that requires two operands to perform an operation.
Here, + is a binary operator because it operates on two operands: 10 and 20.
Arithmetic, comparison, logical AND/OR, and bitwise operators can be binary operators.

A ternary operator requires three operands.

8. What are arithmetic operators in Java?
Arithmetic operators are used to perform mathematical operations.
These are binary operators because they require two operands.
9. What is the difference between the division operator / and modulus operator %?
Both / and % are related to division, but they produce different results.

11. What is the assignment operator in Java?
It assigns the result of the expression on the right side to the variable on the left side.
Here, a + b is evaluated first and its result is assigned to c.
12. What does right-to-left associativity mean for the assignment operator?
The assignment operator works from right to left.
The expression a + b is evaluated first. If a is 10 and b is 20, the result is 30, and that result is assigned to c.
Thus, the value produced on the right side is assigned to the variable on the left side.

19. What are comparison operators in Java?
Comparison operators, also called relational operators, compare two values.
They are binary operators because each comparison requires two operands.
20. What is the result of a comparison operation?
The operands of a comparison operation can be numbers, but the result is Boolean.
21. How does the equality operator == work?
The == operator checks whether two operands have equal values.

22. What does the greater-than operator > check?
The > operator checks whether the left operand is greater than the right operand.
23. What does the less-than operator < check?
The < operator checks whether the left operand is less than the right operand.
24. What do the <= and >= operators check?
The <= operator checks whether the left operand is less than or equal to the right operand.
The >= operator checks whether the left operand is greater than or equal to the right operand.
= operator checks whether two operands have different values.
26. How many arithmetic and comparison operators are there?
Arithmetic operations produce numerical results, while comparison operations produce Boolean results.
27. What are logical operators in Java?
They are used to perform logical operations on Boolean operands.

Bitwise operators perform operations at the bit level.
Computer memory stores data using binary values represented by 0 and 1. A bitwise operation works on the individual bits of the binary representation.
